query:
¬(A ∧ B) ↔ (¬A ∨ ¬B)
¬(A ∨ B) ↔ (¬A ∧ ¬B)
(A → B) ↔ (¬B → ¬A)
(A → B) ↔ (¬A ∨ B)
(¬A → B) ↔ (A ∨ ¬B)

Which of the above is not logically equivalent to the rest? Provide the full statement that doesn't fit.

tasks.description: Извлечь логические выражения из пользовательского запроса.
Построить логический вывод о эквивалентности логических выражений.

assumptions: Logical expressions can be transformed using logical equivalences.
The equivalence of logical expressions can be established through truth tables or logical identities.
reasoning_steps: Identify the logical expressions that need to be compared for equivalence.
Apply logical identities (such as De Morgan's laws, distributive laws, etc.) to transform the expressions.
Construct truth tables for both expressions to compare their outputs for all possible input values.
Determine if the outputs of both expressions match for all combinations of inputs.
conclusions: If the outputs of both logical expressions are identical for all input combinations, then the expressions are equivalent.
If there is at least one combination of inputs where the outputs differ, then the expressions are not equivalent.
proposed_answer_outline: Define the logical expressions to be analyzed.
List the logical identities that will be used for transformation.
Present the truth tables for both expressions.
Summarize the findings regarding their equivalence.
